answers.text: For the driver texts, three fixed lines every time — drop-off time, pallet count, then damage noted — nothing else mixed in. Same message always gives the same three lines.

I'd have the AI list each call entry as time, customer, topic, outcome in that order, then count how many need a follow-up based on which show 'no resolution' as the outcome. That keeps things consistent between two different people using it.
Something doesn't add up with the finishing time on this one, I think it should be the same day, not the day after like the note says.

96 to 118 comes out at about 23%, not the 20% given, so that number needs correcting. The late-payment rate checks out fine, 9 out of 118 is close enough to 92%. The outstanding balance is split evenly at 29,000 each which adds up to 58,000, but that's said to have held steady even though invoices went up this month, and nobody explains why one moved and the other didn't.

I'd go with Output 2, since it gives the actual numbers, 940 tickets and 827 within SLA, and the working behind the 88%. Output 1 just states the percentage on its own, so there's no way to check it without pulling the source numbers yourself.

I'd go with Email 2 since the volume figures are tied to the PO log, so they can be checked. Email 1 just says we deserve a better rate without giving any numbers to back it up, there's nothing there you could verify. I wouldn't send Email 1 as it is.
1. Vendor pricing — no. 2. Total spend, aggregate — yes, that's fine. 3. Unsigned budget draft — no, not released yet. 4. Datasheet, already public — yes. 5. Home address — no, personal.

The hourly rates and retainer cap I'd keep out of an unvetted tool, that's sensitive to the client relationship. The non-disclosure clause needs care too since it names both parties by name. The general service scope though, I don't see a problem pasting that in, there's nothing sensitive in describing what work is covered.
For the monthly reconciliation I check the two regional totals against the warehouse system before it goes up to my manager, straight after the draft's done.

Step 1 carries risk since a misread invoice PDF puts everything after it on the wrong track. The gate that matters most though is step 4, before the payment note goes out automatically, since that's the point it's hard to undo.
